label: Federated tenant posture
query: What should Lakeshore L0 see that Morgan Street L1 should not automatically see at transaction grain?
answer: My read For Lakeshore Holdings, L0 should see the full, tenant-wide transaction grain needed to run the business and govern risk; Morgan Street L1 should only see a sharply scoped slice of that grain tied to their banner’s remit and only the fields required for their role. The default should be “L0 full; L1 least-privilege per banner/role,” not “L1 inherits L0 everywhere.” Why 1) Tenant scope and Azure posture: Your Intelligence surface is already tenant-scoped on Azure AI Search with a private-plane pilot. That same principle should apply to transaction grain: L0 is cross-tenant; L1 is banner-/entity-scoped unless explicitly elevated. 2) Risk and governance: Lakeshore’s role (holdco) must see: – Group-wide liquidity, treasury, and cash-flow—e.g., Kyriba-backed transaction streams at full grain (bank account, counterparty, instrument, timestamp, amount, routing, reconciliation status). – Enterprise ledgers: all journal lines, subledger entries, and intercompany flows. – Group-level vendor / contract payments, including Kyriba treasury operations, AMS modernization spend, and other capital/opex flows. Morgan Street L1 should not automatically see: – Other portfolio companies’ detailed bank transactions or AR/AP lines. – Parent-level financing, equity, and M&A transactions. – Cross-entity transfer pricing and sensitive counterparty detail beyond what their function needs. Decision fork – Option A (tighter): L1 sees only their legal-entity + function slice at transaction grain; everything else is aggregated. – Option B (looser): L1 can see cross-entity operational transactions but not treasury/financing or counterparty-identifying detail.
